column2: The drawing below is to scale. The plate shape was read from your photo using the cutting-mat grid as a ruler (error about 1-2 mm), and the positions of the motors and parts were measured from your three dry-fit photos (error of a few mm). Result: floor 1 is 39% full, floor 2 62%, floor 3 65% of the usable area, with at least 3 mm between parts and nothing stacked. The only things sticking out past the plate edge are the speaker and the TFT on floor 3 (a few mm, at the waist of the plate), on purpose, because the robot's width is set by the wheels anyway. What a top photo cannot show: the height of each floor, which is why there is a height check step.

Final floor 3 (front on the left of the photo): S3 at the rear, breadboard 2 in the middle, the TFT on the robot's right edge (top of the photo) with the SD slot on top, the speaker on the left edge (bottom of the photo). The MAX98357A and INMP441 in the photo do not have a fixed place yet; the head is still lying down.

Floor 3 (third plate): the S3 board at the rear end with its USB-C port facing sideways, breadboard 2 across in front of it (MAX98357A and INMP441 here), the TFT standing on the right edge with the SD card slot on top, the pan-tilt head with the ESP32-CAM at the front end, the box speaker standing on the left edge, and the STOP button plugged into breadboard 2.

Fit the floor-1 ends of the wires that go up, then label their upper ends: 26 AWG 5 V + GND wire to the 30P board (21 cm (no. 21)) and to the S3 board (23 cm (no. 22)) at the OUT terminals of LM2596 #1, the camera 5 V + GND wire (31 cm (no. 23)) at OUT of LM2596 #2 (Part 4), the battery sense wire (18 cm (no. 24)) at IN+ of LM2596 #1, the servo power wire (26 cm (no. 19)) at WAGO 6V/−6 (Part 2).

Fill the third plate while it is still on the table: the S3 board (together with breadboard 2 and the wiring from Part 3) on 10 mm nylon spacers, the TFT standing on the right edge, screen facing outward and the SD card slot on top so the card is easy to pull out (screen orientation 6), held upright with a small bracket or tied with cable ties to a spacer, breadboard 2 tied with cable ties, the pan-tilt head bolted at the front with the pan axis in the middle of the plate width, and the speaker standing on the left edge, tied with two cable ties through the holes of the left middle wing.

STOP button on breadboard 2: plug the tactile button across the middle gap in empty columns, near the left edge so it is easy to press. Push until its legs are fully in. Attach two 27 cm (no. 28) jumper wires to two diagonal legs, one on each side of the gap. Do not connect the button legs to the red or blue rails of breadboard 2, or to S3 pins: this button belongs to the body on floor 2.

Black GND from LM2596 #1 to the GND of the S3 board power block (not its red 5 V yet). UART (wire 29, 27 cm, longer than a 20 cm jumper: join an F-F with an M-F): D16 → IO17, D17 → IO18, G → G on the S3 board. Camera 5 V wire to the ESP32-CAM; servo power is already at the head.
